questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I actually didn't have many demands in terms of choosing the place. I just knew i wanted to go outside of Europe, and that I wanted a university where I had as many english course options as possible, without being in the United states, Canada or Australia. Therefore, Hong Kong Universoty was ideal, since all courses except a few are taught in english,

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I got very little information about my dorm before arrival, i was just sent an acceptance email and the address. However, when I showed up there was no problem, and I got all the information I needed along the way. In terms of information about school start, there was a bunch of introduction events the entire week before first day of classes, so I got all the useful information almost immediately.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: HKU has an entire department designated to administration exchange students, not just in terms of all the pratical stuff, but also in terms of the students wellbeing and socialising. This department was very easy to contact, but it usually wasn't necessary because they on average made sure to send out 5 daily emails about pratical information as well as social events and so on.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: They had dormitories with both the option of private and double rooms. Furthermore, students could apply for student shared apartments if they weren't accepted to a dorm.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Some of the more expensive dorms apparently had meal arrangements for the students, but most of the dorms just provided a very ill-equiped kitchen. For my entire floor with around 40 people, we had one stovetop, one microwave and a broken toaster-oven. In general, I think it is expected for the students to have their own kitchen stuff if they want to cook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is not very clean and cozy, it is mostly just a place to sleep. However, I would strongly recommend applying for the dorms, since it is by far the cheapest option for housing in Hong Kong. Hong Kong generally has a really really bad housing crisis, so I don't think it would be very fun to try and find something on your own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: So they have an add-drop period system (at least for the second semester). This means that course registration opens on the first day of classes, and then you have to register online for the classes you want, but since the first two weeks are add-drop, you a not secured a spot in any of your chosen courses, until the period is over. This also means that you have the first two weeks to just shop around and try different courses to see what you would like. It can be quit stressful since acceptance to the courses usually depends on if there is enough space.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email the administration of your specific department if you had any doubts about the system.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to take five classes, and I shopped around quite a bit and ended up adding and dropping at least ten different courses during the period, so i would say I was happy with what i ended up with. But you should not be to set on specific courses you want, since a lot of them can have quite the competition in terms of acceptance

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't expect to the courses you decided on before hand, be open to try differnt things, and maybe choose the less popular options if you don't want to stress about getting enough credits.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The workload is quite big, but the academic level is quite like danish high school. So its abit confusing to figure out how much you are expected to do.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At least in the faculty of arts its mostly smaller classes with participation from the students so that a lot like how all of my linguistic courses have been at home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Philosophy of language, Linguistic typology, Psycholinguistics, Cantonese for beginners, World englishes, the physics behind how things work

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I dont really know, it really depends on your interests and your academic direction. But i would say to maybe try taking some courses outside of your specific faculty, since the credits are so low that you need to take at least five to get enough credits

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out is very inexpensive, so thats mostly what you can do since the cooking facilities were pretty bad.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds, sports teams, academic clubs, dance teams, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: For staying just one semester I would not recommend signing up for any clubs, since it takes up a lot of your time, and since its mostly locals in the clubs who are not really interested in being friends with exchange students i would reccomend spending your time going to the multiple differnt events organised by the exchange department for exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Beaches, clubbing, just walking around the city. Hiking the millions of trails. Going to China, which is only 20 minutes by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Because of its history Hong Kong is a very international city, so everything is in english next to the cantonese. Furthermore, most of the locals a pretty used to foreigners, and most also speak english i various levels, so it very easy to get around, and explore the city and get emerged in the culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are pretty hard to get to know, so must exchange students just stick to meeting other exchange students. But if you really want to befriend the locals you should maybe sign up for the clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They tend to d things quite late in the night, so a lot of courses don't finish until nine o'clock at night, and the dorms dont really get quite until like three in the morning.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Just have easy it is to do things by yourself. Going to any restaurant alone is seen a completely normal, however, most of the time you will get seated right next to strangers. Also, it is one of the safest cities to walk around a night by your self.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Talk to as many people as you can. Dont say no to any invitations. And don't spend to much time focusing on academics.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You need to pratice your handwriting since most exams on BA level is dont with pencil and paper.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Everything

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not spending to much money on traveling around the area.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
